newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut treasurer still sees $120 mln surplus.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut treasurer still sees $120 mln surplus.

text.p: The Connecticut State Treasurer, for the third month in a row, said that she expected to see a $120 million surplus in the 1997 fiscal year that ends in June because revenues will outpace spending.

Nancy Wyman increased her estimate of how much general fund spending would total, raising it to $103.8 million more than budgeted, in prepared remarks released on Thursday. In early December, the state comptroller had looked for spending to be only about $81.5 million above budget.

The higher spending was due to Medicaid, which was $47.4 million over budget, and care for children in foster and residential care, which was $30.7 million over budget. Wyman said she asked the Department of Social Services to explain the Medicaid overruns, as costs had been projected to drop due to managed care.
Income tax collections now are projected at $125 million over budget, rising with the national economy's rebound, "booming financial markets," and state job growth, Wyman said.
Sales tax collections will rise by $98.3 million, she predicted.
